source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.215
purpose: Boundaries that any downstream use of this material must respect. Recorded from the source text only; no correctness judgement is made here and no formula is repaired.

necessary_conditions.item: Genericity of the k-tuple of conjugacy classes
necessary_conditions.content: Definition 3.2 (def_generic_class): (1) the product of ALL eigenvalues occurring in the multiset union of the Delta(sigma^j) equals 1; (2) for every 1 <= r <= n-1 and every choice of subsets R_j of Delta(sigma^j) with |R_j| = r, the product of the chosen eigenvalues is different from 1.
necessary_conditions.must_keep: Both conditions; the fact (line 1056) that genericity depends only on the eigenvalues and their multiplicities nu^j_r, not on the Jordan types mu.
necessary_conditions.do_not_strengthen_or_weaken: This is a single global product condition on all eigenvalues, NOT the condition that each individual class lies in SL_n (determinant 1 per puncture). It must not be replaced by a per-puncture determinant condition, and the r <= n-1 restriction and the 'subset of size exactly r in every Delta' quantifier must be kept.

necessary_conditions.item: Fixed rank n and fixed genus g with k distinct punctures
necessary_conditions.content: Sigma compact Riemann surface of genus g, Sigma^0 = Sigma minus {p_1,...,p_k}, n-dimensional representations; g non-negative integer, k positive integer.
necessary_conditions.must_keep: n fixed; k >= 1; g = 0 is included (Theorem 5.3 and the middle-convolution paragraph 2200 are explicitly the g = 0 case).

necessary_conditions.item: Group is GL_n with a PGL_n quotient (not SL_n, not an arbitrary reductive group)
necessary_conditions.content: The variety is the GIT quotient by PGL_n of the GL_n-representation space; at 1893 and in Section 4 the author notes a larger family of groups was treated by Biquard-Garcia-Prada-Mundet i Riera, but the results here are for GL_n.
necessary_conditions.must_keep: GL_n with the PGL_n quotient; the PGL_n rather than GL_n quotient is what makes the action free under genericity.

necessary_conditions.content: K is C or an algebraic closure of a finite field; l-adic coefficients qlbar; over C, mixed Hodge structures exist by Saito.
necessary_conditions.must_keep: For singular character varieties the main5.2formula is compactly supported IH_c with the stated coefficient conventions. The smooth resolution/semisimple twisted5.5/5.6formulas use ordinary compactly supported H_c; smoothness identifies IH_c and H_c. Keep each object separately.
necessary_conditions.producer_must_keep: The Poincare polynomial is that of COMPACTLY SUPPORTED intersection cohomology IH_rc (subscript rc), with l-adic coefficients; it is not ordinary cohomology and not IH without compact support.

necessary_conditions.item: Resolution is used through a diffeomorphism, not an algebraic isomorphism
necessary_conditions.content: Theorem 4.1: M-tilde_{L,P,sigma} is DIFFEOMORPHIC to a character variety M_S with semisimple classes. Line 2103 additionally says the map p^{sigma-tilde} of Definition 3.6 is an isomorphism between M-tilde_{L,P,sigma-tilde} and M_S for the perturbed parameter sigma-tilde.
necessary_conditions.must_keep: Keep the distinction: the comparison of Poincare polynomials uses only the diffeomorphism (lines 2140-2143: 'the Poincare polynomial is a topological invariant'); do not upgrade the general statement to an algebraic isomorphism, and do not silently drop the perturbed-parameter isomorphism at 2103.

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.item: Objects quantified over in the main statement
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.content: For a generic k-tuple of conjugacy classes C_{mu,sigma}: mu = (underline mu^1,...,underline mu^k) with underline mu^j = (mu^{j,1},...,mu^{j,l_j}) and mu^{j,i} a partition of nu^j_i; sigma^j diagonal with distinct eigenvalues sigma^j_r of multiplicity nu^j_r.
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.must_keep: The partition data and eigenvalue multiplicities; s_{mu'} = prod_j prod_i s_{{mu^{j,i}}'}[X_j] (definition at 1238-1240); the primed (transposed) partition convention from Notations 2.8.

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.content: dim M_{bar C_{mu,sigma}} = d_mu := n^2(2g-2) + 2 + sum_j dim C_{underline mu^j, sigma^j}, valid when the variety is non-empty (Proposition 3.5).
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.must_keep: Exactly this normalisation of d_mu; it is the exponent in v^{d_mu} in Theorems 1.1, 5.2 and in the twisted statements. Note that Theorem 5.5 uses d_mu (the dimension attached to mu, not to rho) although the object is the resolution.

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.content: H_n^{HLV}(z,w) := (z^2-1)(1-w^2) Log Omega_k^g(z,w) restricted to s^n; the pairing is the Hall pairing <,> with <p_lambda,p_mu> = delta_{lambda,mu} z_lambda (519-521); the evaluation point is (-1,v).
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.must_keep: The degree-n restriction, the (z^2-1)(1-w^2) prefactor, the Hall pairing normalisation and the argument (-1,v); genus g and number of punctures k enter through Omega_k^g.
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.producer_must_keep: The degree-n restriction, the (z^2-1)(1-w^2) prefactor, the Hall pairing normalisation (not the Schur orthonormal normalisation) and the argument (-1,v); genus g and number of punctures k enter through Omega_k^g.
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.owner_note: The stated Hall pairing and Schur orthonormality are compatible; do not invent an opposed normalization.

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.content: The Poincare polynomial of the empty variety is defined to be 0; Theorem 5.2 is asserted to remain valid in the empty case, with the equivalence chain at 2191-2193 and the vanishing of N_{lambda',mu'} outside the dominance region (Macdonald [I-6]).
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.must_keep: The convention 'P_rc(empty) = 0' and the fact that the empty case is covered by the proof's final paragraph; do not state the formula only for non-empty varieties.

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.content: For semisimple classes mu^{j,i} = (1^{nu^j_i}), so s_{mu'} = prod_j h_{nu^j}[X_j] = h_nu, and M_S is smooth so IH = ordinary cohomology; this is Mellit's case (Theorem 3.13).
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.must_keep: The specialisation s_{(nu)} = h_nu is what makes the two formulas agree; do not present the semisimple formula as a corollary proved here (it is an external input, lines 283 and 1274).

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.content: p^sigma_! kappa[d_mu] decomposes with summands A_{mu',rho} tensor IC of M_{bar C_{rho,sigma}}, and in cohomology H^{i+d_mu}_rc(M-tilde) = oplus A_{mu',rho} tensor IH^{i+d_rho}_rc(M_{bar C_{rho,sigma}}).
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.must_keep: The two DIFFERENT shifts d_mu on the resolution side and d_rho on the intersection-cohomology side; the variance t^{-d_mu} P_rc(M_S,t) = sum (dim A_{mu',rho}) t^{-d_rho} P_rc(M_{bar C_{rho,sigma}},t) at 2146 (with the variable named both t and v across 2142-2147).

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.content: A_{mu',rho} = Hom_{W_M}(Ind_{W_L}^{W_M} eps_{mu'}, V_rho) and dim A_{mu',rho} = prod_{j,i} <h_{{mu^{j,i}}'}, s_{{rho^{j,i}}'}>.
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.must_keep: Induction from W_L, the sign representation eps_{mu'} (not the trivial one), and the tensor-product factorisation over punctures and blocks.

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.content: eta indexes a conjugacy class in the relative Weyl group W_M(L); the sign (-1)^{r(eta)} and the symmetric function h-tilde_eta are those of Notations 3.9 (1176-1199).
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.must_keep: The relative Weyl group (permutations of equal-sized blocks of L, 969-977), the r(eta) parity sign, and h-tilde_eta = prod s_{{omega_eta}'} evaluated in the variables X_j.

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.content: Weighted Sobolev classes L^{k,2}_delta with the splitting End(E) = End(E)_0 + End(E)_1; admissibility a in L^{1,2}_{-2+delta}; the variation requires 0 < delta < beta_i - beta_j locally (1808-1810) and 0 < delta-tilde < delta - max_{i,j}|eps_i - eps_j| globally (2054-2057), where eps_i = alpha-tilde_i - alpha_i.
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.must_keep: The strict inequalities and the -2+delta shift; the local and global delta are DIFFERENT parameters (explicitly said at 2054-2055). These are the quantitative conditions under which Theorem 4.33 is proved.

quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.content: The full mixed Hodge polynomial statements are Conjectures 3.12 and 3.15 (unproved). Only the Poincare specialisations are theorems here (5.2 and 5.5).
quantifiers_regularity_objects_limits_no.must_keep: Do not attribute an ordinary/mixed Hodge or E-polynomial theorem to this paper; the E-polynomial specialisations are cited external results (lines 1252-1255).

producer_core_recount_boundary.rule_applied: One core per construction; tools, weakenings and direct applications are not split into separate candidates.
boundaries: Theorem 4.1 and the Section 4 chain (Proposition 4.18; Definition 4.25 and Remark 4.26; Theorems 4.27-4.31; Proposition 4.32; Theorem 4.33) form ONE geometric construction, already counted by the old 2147 H3 judgement. Do not re-count its pieces.
Theorem 5.5 and Corollary 5.6 are direct applications of Theorem 5.2 combined with the existing trace formula (Theorem 3.10) and Lemma 2.29; they differ in statement but not in core.
Theorem 4.11 (with Propositions 4.2, 4.7, 4.10 and Theorems 4.3) is the n=2, k=4 illustration of the same diffeomorphism, proved with classical surface theory; not an independent advanced core.
Lemma 5.1, Lemma 2.15, Lemma 2.29, Theorem 2.34 and Theorem 3.10 are supporting tools of the single computation.

The Mellit formula (Theorem 3.13), the Letellier decomposition (Theorem 3.8), the Springer/Borho-MacPherson/Lusztig results and all Biquard-Boalch/Simpson/Yamakawa/Konno analytic constructions are named external inputs and are not author proofs.
